newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher after sharp LME stock dip.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher after sharp LME stock dip.

text.p: COMEX copper bounced back Tuesday after the heavy, fund-led selloff of Monday.
The market was helped by a sharp fall in LME stocks overnight, mainly from Singapore which may indicate Chinese interest in the market, dealers said.
Trading was quiet for much of the day, with the major move upward taking place at and just after the opening.
"We have had a pretty good selloff in the market and we were due for a bit of a bounce," William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said.
LME stocks Tuesday fell 6,475 tonnes to 167,125 tonnes.
"The stock draw was a bit supportive because it showed a big draw out of Singapore," O'Neill added.
May COMEX copper settled up 2.15 cents at 106.90 cents a lb after trading from 106.90 to 105.30 cents. Spot April went out 1.95 cents higher at 108.45 cents.
Volume was estimated at 7,500 lots compared to Monday's official 11,779 lots.

Meanwhile, the United Steelworkers of America union said it was due to meet Phelps Dodge on April 24 and 25 to resume labor talks at the Chino mine in New Mexico where workers have been without contract since June 30, 1996.
